subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Solve problems in context to 25
source.subtopic: Equal grouping and sharing leading to division that may include remainders (weeks 3-8)

show.line: Share fairly! Eight sweets for two friends. One for you, one for me. Each friend gets four.

rounds.prompt: Six apples shared between two children. Count how many each child gets.
rounds.praise: Three each! Six shared by two is three.

rounds.story: Gogo has ten oranges. She shares them between five grandchildren. How many does each one get?
rounds.praise: Two each! Ten shared by five is two.

rounds.prompt: Twelve eggs go into boxes of four. Count the boxes.
Nine biscuits shared between three friends. How many each? Say the number.

rounds.story: Sipho has seven marbles. He shares them fairly between two friends. How many marbles are left over?
rounds.praise: One left over! Each friend gets three, and one is left.

rounds.prompt: Which picture shows eight blocks shared equally into two groups?
rounds.praise: Yes! Four and four. That is fair.

hints: Give one to each, then one more to each, until they are all gone.
Fair means every group has the same number.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will share eight sweets between two friends.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Five for you, three for me. Fair!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! Five and three is not fair. Four and four is fair.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's share together. One for you, one for me, until they are gone. Four each!

parent_line: Can share objects equally and say how many are left over.
